pilot: ARIS4C015 Pilot M 500-paper merged OpenAlex mechanism cohort
interpretation: Merging five reproducible random shards before normalization yielded 497 unique historical papers and zero robust Sleeping Beauty cases.
Twenty-two papers showed low-early/high-late trajectories but failed at least one robust retrospective SB component.
The random cohort already contains abundant Forgotten and Immediate-Hit controls; the limiting resource is robust SB case yield.

Random sampling should therefore not be scaled merely to wait for rare Sleeping Beauties. The mechanism track should switch to case-enriched retrospective extraction, then sample matched controls from the population.
design_decision: Stop scaling random mechanism sampling. Use SciSciNet-v2 case enrichment for Track M; retain random cohorts only for Track B prospective evaluation.
claim_boundary: Yield diagnostic from one field/year and five random shards; not an estimate of global Sleeping Beauty prevalence.
